issues.description: Class property naming mismatch for the Course instructor: the problem statement and template define a Course property and initializer parameter named 'instructor' (used as the course's instructor), but the solution's Course implementation declares the property and initializer parameter as 'lecturer'. At the same time, other solution artifacts (Developer.attend and Client) still reference 'instructor'. This cross-artifact naming inconsistency (Course.lecturer vs Course.instructor) will cause compilation errors and will confuse students trying to map the reference implementation to the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the Course property and initializer parameter in the solution from 'lecturer' to 'instructor' in Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift, and update any references (for example in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift and Client.swift) to use course.instructor. Alternatively, if 'lecturer' is desired, update the problem statement and the template to use 'lecturer' consistently and adjust all call sites accordingly. Ensure the final names match so the code compiles and aligns with the exercise text.
